subject: Business Models
title: Franchise Resale Market
description: A short lesson to help you apply Franchise Resale Market.

hook.text: A successful McDonald's franchise can sell for 1.5-2x its annual revenue. That's $3-6 million.

buildup.text: Franchise resale is a secondary market where existing operators sell their locations to new buyers.

discovery.text: Resale values reflect actual performance, not franchisor projections. It's the most honest valuation.

twist.text: Franchisors have 'right of first refusal'—they can block any buyer they don't approve of.

climax.text: The resale market is crucial: it creates exit options for franchisees who want to cash out.

punchline.text: Build it, sell it for millions. The resale market rewards strong operators.

quiz.question: What does 'right of first refusal' mean in franchise resales?
options: Franchisees must sell at a set price
The franchisor can block unapproved buyers

details.summary: The franchise resale market lets existing franchisees sell their operating businesses to new buyers, often at valuations based on a multiple of earnings..
details.whyItMatters: Resales represent both exit strategy for existing franchisees and lower-risk entry for new ones. Understanding resale dynamics reveals how franchise investments create or destroy equity and why some franchise brands command premium resale multiples.
takeaways: Resale buyers acquire operating businesses with existing revenue and customer bases
Valuations are typically 2 to 5 times annual earnings for profitable franchise locations
Franchisors must approve all transfers and may charge transfer fees of 5,000 to 25,000

faq.question: What determines the resale value of a franchise?
faq.answer: Profitability and earnings trend, remaining years on the franchise agreement, location quality, required upcoming renovations, brand strength and system-wide performance, local market growth potential, and the general supply and demand for that particular franchise brand.

faq.question: Why do some franchise brands have higher resale values than others?
faq.answer: Strong brands with high unit economics, growing customer demand, supportive corporate culture, and long franchise agreement terms command premium multiples. Brands with declining sales, frequent encroachment, high renovation costs, or short remaining agreement terms have depressed resale values.
